answer: An identity protocol counters Sybil attacks by binding each agent to an actuated laser mirror located in an outdoor sensor garden. A verifier transmits modulated optical pulses and evaluates sub-millimeter angular deflections in the reflection to prove physical actuation. An attacker must procure, calibrate, and power discrete steering hardware for every identity. However, intense wind buffeting from a gale can shake the optical mount, causing legitimate agents to fail verification.
